definition: Naomi Sager (born 1927) is an American computational linguistics research scientist.
details: She is a former research professor at New York University, now retired. She is a pioneer in the development of natural language processing for computers.

explainer.lead: Naomi Sager is a Computational linguistics expert.

contributions.name: Her work in linguistics led her to New York University, where she collaborated with James Morris and Morris Salkoff to develop a parsing program based on natural language processing.

timeline.what: Sager was born in Chicago, Illinois in 1927.
She obtained a Bachelor of Science in electrical engineering from Columbia University in 1953.
In 1965 NYU launched the Linguistic String Project under Sager's leadership.
Sager managed the project for 30 years until her retirement in 1995.

affiliations: Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science
